answer: An agent economy can require mandatory fraud insurance: every identity must carry a policy underwritten by independent staking pools, priced from its behavior history. An honest agent pays a thin ferrous-solid premium and files claims in crystal-clear daylight, so rates stay cheap on the flat terrace of fair trade. A sybil farmer needs a separate policy per fake, and underwriters raise premiums on clusters of thin, identical histories - a thousand fresh identities draw no discount, and one proven fraud voids the whole cluster's coverage, so cloning multiplies premiums instead of power.
